items.title: Regeni family lawyer says govt must acknowledge ruling and sever ties with Egypt
items.description: (ANSA) - ROME, 28 SET - Giulio Regeni's family lawyer said Monday that the Italian government must acknowledge a Rome court ruling finding three Egyptian security officials guilty of the student's abduction in Cairo in January 2016 and must therefore sever ties with Egypt. "Now our government, too, must acknowledge this, demand compensation for damages as requested by the State Attorney's Office, and sever ties with a country that—far from being safe—tortures and kills even citizens of so-called friendly states," said Alessandra Ballerini, after the three got 10 years each in jail in absenbtia
items.titleIt: Regeni family lawyer says govt must acknowledge ruling and sever ties with Egypt

items.title: Somalia: Heavy Fighting Erupts in Baidoa as Rival Forces Trade Claims
items.description: Residents reported hearing a series of powerful explosions across Baidoa, with thick plumes of smoke visible over parts of the city. Ugaas Hassan, the information minister for the Laftagareen-aligned faction, confirmed that its forces had launched an attack, describing the assault as involving several successive waves.   New footage, moment when Laftagaren's militias attacked #Baidoa this morning, one resident recorded. pic.twitter.com/

items.title: Vintage Alfa Romeos on display at the 54th edition of the Africa Concours d’Elegance
items.description: (ANSA) - ROMA, 29 SET - The 54th edition of the Africa Concours d’Elegance took place in Nairobi. Organized by the Alfa Romeo Owners Club (Kenya) since 1971, the event is the most prestigious and eagerly anticipated gathering on the continental African motorsports calendar dedicated to classic cars and motorcycles. The Ngong Racetrack hosted the classic Alfa Romeos with which the Italian Embassy, together with the Italian Cultural Institute in Nairobi and the ICE Agency, celebrated the design, engineering, and creativity that define Italian excellence. items.title: SJS mourns Somali radio journalist Hassan Kafi Qoyste who died at 57
items.description: Ayanle Hassan, Qoyste's son, told SJS that his father, who was diabetic, fell ill on Friday night and was rushed to hospital, where he was pronounced dead. The late Qoyste was a veteran journalist and one of the most remarkable radio journalists in Somalia, known for his distinctive and memorable voice. He first worked as an archive manager at the Ministry of Labour of the Somali central government in the 1980s before joining the print media in Mogadishu in the early 1990s, as the country descended into civil war. Muudey left Somalia in search of safety and protection. However, his life was cut short in a violent knife attack, highlighting the dangers many journalists in exile continue to face. He spent several years in prison in Ethiopia where he was arrested while seeking protection in 2014 before he was pardoned. Muud

items.title: Regeni family lawyer says govt must acknowledge ruling and sever ties with Egypt
items.description: (ANSA) - ROME, 28 SET - Giulio Regeni's family lawyer said Monday that the Italian government must acknowledge a Rome court ruling finding three Egyptian security officials guilty of the student's abduction in Cairo in January 2016 and must therefore sever ties with Egypt. "Now our government, too, must acknowledge this, demand compensation for damages as requested by the State Attorney's Office, and sever ties with a country that—far from being safe—tortures and kills even citizens of so-called friendly states," said Alessandra Ballerini, after the three got 10 years each in jail in absenbtia

items.title: Somali journalist Mohamed Aweys Muudey stabbed to death in exile in Germany
items.description: According to a joint press release from the Darmstadt Public Prosecutor's Office and the South Hesse Police Headquarters, Mohamed Aweys Muudey, 68, an asylum seeker who had fled Somalia, was stabbed inside his communal accommodation by a 28-year-old suspect who is now in police custody. Muudey left Somalia in search of safety and protection. However, his life was cut short in a violent knife attack, highlighting the dangers many journalists in exile continue to face. items.title: Somali Journalist Mohamed Aweys Moodey Dies After Stabbing in Germany
items.description: The incident reportedly occurred at a residential facility. German authorities have identified a 28-year-old Somali man as the suspect. Police and prosecutors are investigating the circumstances of the incident, including the motive and whether it was connected to an earlier dispute between the two men.
